messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@finexahealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: consolidated vendor score snapshot + next tests

Hi Priya / Samir —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our end so we have aligned action items and measurable tests for the evaluation committee. I pulled together a one-sheet score snapshot (attached) that combines the items you called out on the demo: throughput at peak, hallucination surface for clinical templates, redaction controls, and procurement/operational fit.

Top pain points you reiterated:
- Variable latency at high concurrency causing timeouts in triage UI (esp. 400–600 concurrent sessions).
- Sensitive PHI/PII handling and need for provable in-flight redaction + audit logs.
- Cost predictability for burst windows (end of day claims processing).

Primary goals we confirmed:
1) Maintain sub-300ms median token latency for typical triage prompts and <800ms 95th at 200 concurrent users.
2) Zero exposure of PHI in logs and a KMS-backed key workflow for model requests.
3) Predictable unit economics under peak (target <= $0.012/token for production mix).

Decision criteria (weighted in attached matrix): reliability (35%), security/compliance (25%), cost (20%), integration effort (10%), vendor support SLA (10%). Camila and Karthik — I included your proposed weights in the spreadsheet but can update based on the committee.

Open questions we promised to answer (short list):
- Can you confirm the types of PII you must redact (SSNs, MRNs, DOB, provider notes) so we scope the redaction test?
- What does your burst profile look like in Q4 — is 600 concurrent an upper bound or to be used for stress tests?
- Procurement timeline and PO approval owner (for target December rollout).

Proposed next tests (we suggest running these over the coming two weeks):
A) Ingestion + redaction smoke: we will run a 100k-record synthetic ingest with your PII schema and demonstrate end-to-end redaction and audit traces. (Owner: Redwood — Marissa / Camila)
B) Latency stress: 4-hour ramp to 600 concurrent sessions on a production-like prompt mix; capture med/95/99 latencies and failure modes. (Owner: Finexa infra / Redwood ops support)
C) Quality probe: 50 clinical templates run against latest open model variants with expected answer set to measure hallucination/error rate. (Owner: Finexa clinical + Redwood research)

Next steps / timeline:
- I’ll upload the scorecard and decision matrix to the shared Drive tonight.
- Can you confirm by EOD Tue which PII fields to include and whether the compliance team needs an NDA addendum for sample data?
- We propose kicking off A + B on Wed (9/14) if procurement permits.

Attaching: redwood-vs-competitors-scorecard.xlsx (score snapshot), decision-matrix-priorities.pdf. Also linking the call recording.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for this crisp summary and the spreadsheet. A few clarifications from our side: we will include SSN, MRN, DOB, and provider free-text notes in the redaction set. We do not need DOB truncation, we want full redaction.

Burst profile: 600 concurrent is an aggressive upper bound. Typical peak is ~250–300, but we want to validate to 600 for safety. Q4 windows are usually 2–3 hours each night (around 10pm–1am PT) — that's our main cost concern.

Procurement timeline: we will aim to have the PO approved by 11/30; the procurement owner is Samir and I will loop our legal for the NDA addendum (Samir, please advise if we need a vendor DPA addendum).

We are good to proceed with tests A and B on 9/14 as long as Redwood provides a test plan and the redaction bin schema by EOD 9/13. One quick ask: can Redwood also include a lightweight ingestion tool (script + sample mapping) so we can run the ingest step on our infra?

Looking forward — Priya
Director, Data Platform
Finexa Health
priya@finexahealth.com
